gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.title: Missing %s Data
gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.body: Your %1$s are missing. %2$s can put them back.
gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.why: They were most likely deleted by a modpack update, which replaces the config folder they used to live in. These are the places they might still exist:
Restores the first entry listed. Only adds files that are missing — nothing you have now is changed or deleted.
gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.done.bod: Put back %1$s file(s). Your %2$s should be there again.
gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.done.not: Nothing was missing — every file was already there.
gui.dungeonbackup.data_recovery.done.fai: The restore couldn't finish — see the game log. Nothing was changed or deleted.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups.tip: Restore points of your saved data. Cycle through the options to see what each one protects against.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups.overri: Forced to '%s' by a launch flag (-Ddungeonbackup.backups). Remove the flag to change it here.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups.extern: Backup outside the instance, so updates won't touch them. Also survives the instance being deleted or reset.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups.instan: Back up inside the instance. Likely safe from a modpack update, but not always — and deleting or resetting the instance will delete the backups.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups.off.ti: No backups. If your saved data is lost, there is nothing to restore from.
gui.dungeonbackup.options.backups_per_ve: How many backups to keep for each mod version. Older ones for that version are removed once there are more. Lowering this deletes archives you already have, the next time a backup is written.
Delete every backup to free the space. Your saved data itself is not touched — but if you lose it later, there will be nothing to restore from.
